title: sse: fix streaming chunking/framing for partial JSON, delimiter ordering, and token/event ordering
author: Evan Brooks
description:
Motivation: We observed two classes of streaming regressions when customers consumed SSE-style streaming in OpenAI-compatible mode: 1) partial JSON objects could be split across chunk boundaries and the delimiter/token ordering in adapter layers caused malformed partial-json delivery; 2) race between token events and delimiter events (e.g. '

' vs token payload) resulted in out-of-order token/metadata events in some client buffer implementations. This PR fixes the chunking/framing logic in the server-side SSE stream parser and the OpenAI compatibility adapter to preserve event ordering and ensure partial JSON objects are reassembled before the `data: ` line is emitted. Summary of changes: - server: stabilize sse stream_parser to accumulate incomplete JSON frames in a small buffer keyed by stream id and emit only complete JSON or valid partial-json with explicit continuation markers - openai_compat: change streaming_adapter to prefer delimiter-aware flushing and attach ordering metadata to intermediate events so downstream clients can reassemble in-order - client shim: add a defensive reorder-by-seq fallback for known flaky clients (opt-in, behind feature flag) - tests: add extensive unit/integration tests that simulate TCP fragmentation, chunked transfer encoding boundaries, and concurrent token vs delimiter emissions - docs: update streaming compatibility notes with recommended client behavior and a migration note for older SDKs Compatibility: the changes are backwards-compatible for well-behaved clients; for clients that parsed by naive line-splitting, we added a short migration note and opt-in shim to aid rollouts. CI: initial test run failed on an existing flaky SSE test; reran the job and all checks passed. Incident context: this PR fixes regressions surfaced by SUP-9082 where a high-volume customer observed malformed JSON objects in streaming responses. Related PRs: ENG-3201 improvements to KV-cache routing that increased concurrency and exposed a race in the SSE path.
commits: Fix: accumulate partial JSON frames before emitting SSE data lines
OpenAI compat: delimiter-aware flush and ordering metadata
Add: integration tests for TCP fragmentation and chunk boundaries
Tests: add deterministic token/delimiter race harness
Docs: streaming compatibility and migration note
diff_snippets: stream_parser.rs: buffer incomplete JSON chunks keyed by stream_id and add assemble_partial() helper
streaming_adapter.py: added OrderedEvent with seq metadata and flush_on_delimiter flag
sse_shim.ts: opt-in reorder-by-seq fallback behind feature flag 'sse_strict_ordering'
test_sse_fragmentation.py: simulate chunk sizes 1..512 and assert final reassembled JSON equals expected payload

Evan Brooks: added inline comment and expanded unit test to cover the '+

' edge case
Gabriel Ortiz: Left a small suggestion to reduce allocations in assemble_partial(); prefer using BytesMut here
Evan Brooks: switched to BytesMut and added benchmark notes in code comments
Hannah Liu: Approving after tests and CI green. Suggest we add a follow-up to remove the opt-in shim once SDKs are upgraded: ENG-3201
ci_summary: CI: linux-unit (passed), linux-integration (passed after rerun), python-lint (passed), go-lint (passed), wasm (skipped), benchmarks (informational). One flaky test on first run (test_sse_ordering) was retried and passed.
merge_outcome: PR merged to main via squash. Release notes updated for 2026-02 patch release.
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming partial-JSON and delimiter/token ordering regressions. Customers using streaming APIs may see improved stability for OpenAI-compatible streams. No API changes. Migration note: clients that split on naive line boundaries should follow updated streaming_compat.md recommendations.
notes: Rollout plan: feature flag 'sse_strict_ordering' enabled for canary traffic for 48hrs, then 100% rollout. Follow-up: remove opt-in shim after SDKs 1.14+ are adopted (ENG-3201).
testing: Added both unit and integration tests that reproduce TCP fragmentation and token/delimiter races; local benchmarks show negligible latency impact (<1ms p50) and minor CPU increase under pathological fragmentation tests.
